title: The Case of the Loose Mooring
story: Frost silvered the town pier one November morning, the week before haul-out, when someone untied Felix's sailboat, the Ripple, and let her drift onto Gull Rock. She has a scraped keel; Felix has a long face. Five early risers came down to the dock, each at a different time, in a different coat, on a different errand. A dog walker on the seawall saw someone in a yellow slicker bent over the Ripple's mooring line. Who untied the Ripple?

texts: The person in the fleece arrived half an hour after the person who came for mail.
Of Hal and the person in the barn coat, one arrived at 6:30 a.m. and the other arrived at 7:00 a.m.
The person who arrived at 7:00 a.m. came for neither bait nor mail.
Of the person in the peacoat and the person who came for mail, one is Walt and the other is Hal.
The person who arrived at 8:00 a.m. came for either diesel or mail.
The person in the slicker came for neither bait nor coffee.
Quinn did not wear the slicker.
Of the person who came for mail and the person who arrived at 8:00 a.m., one wore the fleece and the other wore the parka.
The person who came for coffee is either Walt or Bea.
